terra.problem: It assigns a reason for Amos’s choice of words that the text does not give, even though the reason is marked as a guess.
It claims nobody is checking the locks and imagines the people sleeping with the door open. The verse gives neither detail.
Being at ease and distinguished does not establish that the people are not hungry or worn out.
The verse says they bring violence near, not that they welcome it. The explanation has also already covered the whole verse when it refers to the rest of it.
The text does not say the lambs and calves are the best of the flock and stall.
It invents a preference for the people, suggesting they would turn up their noses at a plain loaf. The text does not say that.
The verse does not say the people are used to being served.
David is introduced as a king without a reference for that fact outside this passage.
The text says they invent instruments, not that they build them to play their songs on.
The text says they invent instruments, not that they build them. The garage joke also places a modern detail in the biblical crowd rather than making a separate comparison.
Failing to grieve over the ruin is not necessarily the same as ignoring it. The text does not say the ruin went ignored.
The passage does not say whether the ivory beds go with them into exile.
Being taken captive does not establish that someone has not been fighting.
The table comparison has no clear joke logic and suggests pride and weakness cannot coexist.
The line about a big sentence in a short verse makes the way Scripture is written the joke.
Saying there are no jokes here comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
The verse calls it the fruit of righteousness; it does not say justice is that fruit.
The passage describes feasting but does not state that the people had not turned their feasts into fasting.
It identifies the boast as the same pride named in verse 8, a connection the passage does not explicitly make.
